title: Chapter 1.  Geography — Location, Physiography & the Trans-Himalayan Ranges

blocks.content: Ladakh is India's highest-altitude and most sparsely populated Union Territory, and its geography chapter is dominated by one central theme: it lies almost entirely in the 'Trans-Himalaya' — the belt of ranges north of the main Himalayan watershed, on the Tibetan-plateau side — giving it a fundamentally different climate, ecology and strategic character from the rest of India.

Ladakh lies in the extreme north of India, bordered by the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir to the west, Himachal Pradesh to the south, and by two international frontiers of major strategic significance: the Line of Control (LoC) with Pakistan-administered territory to the north-west, and the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China to the north and east.

It is India's largest Union Territory by area and among the least densely populated territories in the entire country, a direct consequence of its extreme altitude, cold-desert climate, and difficult terrain, which together support only a thin scatter of population concentrated in river valleys and oasis-like irrigated pockets.

Ladakh's location at the junction of the Karakoram, the Western Himalaya and the Tibetan plateau made it historically a crucial node on trans-Asian trade routes connecting India, Central Asia, Tibet and China — a role reflected today in its rich, multi-directional cultural heritage (Chapter 10).

cells: approx 59,146 sq km - India's LARGEST Union Territory by area
Line of Control (LoC) with Pakistan-administered territory (north-west); Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China (north/east)
approx 3,000 m, rising to over 7,000 m at the highest peaks

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Ladakh is India's LARGEST Union Territory by area (~59,146 sq km) but one of the smallest by population - a frequently tested contrast, and a useful complement to remembering Delhi as one of the smallest-by-area, most-densely-populated UTs.

Unlike the Kashmir Valley and Jammu region (which lie on the monsoon-facing southern side of the main Himalayan watershed), Ladakh lies almost entirely on the northern, rain-shadow side, in the belt of ranges collectively termed the Trans-Himalaya - making its mountain geography, climate and ecology fundamentally distinct from the rest of the erstwhile combined state.

cells: Forms Ladakh's southern/western boundary, dividing it from the Kashmir Valley (crossed via Zoji La) and from Zanskar's own high valleys
Major glacier-source range; the historic barrier separating monsoon-fed Kashmir from Ladakh's cold desert
Runs through central Ladakh, separating the Zanskar valley from the Indus valley
Extremely rugged, high-altitude terrain; source of the Zanskar River
Runs roughly parallel to and north of the Indus River, between the Indus and Shyok valleys
Trans-Himalayan range; contributes to Ladakh's rain-shadow, cold-desert character
Forms Ladakh's northern frontier, adjoining the LAC with China and the LoC-adjacent areas near Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan
Extremely high-altitude range; hosts the Siachen Glacier and numerous peaks exceeding 7,000-8,000 m

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Remember the stacking specific to Ladakh: Great Himalaya/Zanskar (southern boundary) -> Zanskar Range (central) -> Indus Valley (the settled core) -> Ladakh Range -> Shyok Valley -> Karakoram Range (northern frontier). This full sequence is a favourite exam ordering question.

cells: Highest peak substantially within Ladakh's Karakoram range, exceeding 7,600 m
One of the world's highest motorable passes (~5,359 m, though older claims of ~5,602 m are now considered inaccurate by modern GPS survey); gateway from Leh to the Nubra Valley and Siachen approach
High pass (~5,360 m) on the route from Leh to Pangong Tso
Connects Ladakh (via Dras/Kargil) to the Kashmir Valley (via Sonamarg); covered in detail in the companion J&K GS volume
Highest point on the Srinagar-Leh highway within Ladakh's Kargil-Leh stretch

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Khardung La is frequently (though not always precisely) cited as 'one of the world's highest motorable passes' - a very commonly tested superlative, though modern GPS measurements have revised its exact altitude downward from older, inflated figures still seen on some roadside signage.

items: Ladakh: approx 59,146 sq km - India's LARGEST UT by area; 2 districts (Leh, Kargil); borders J&K (UT) and Himachal Pradesh, plus the LoC (Pakistan) and LAC (China).
Almost entirely in the Trans-Himalaya (rain-shadow, north of the main Himalayan watershed) - fundamentally different from Kashmir Valley/Jammu's monsoon-facing geography.
Key ranges: Great Himalaya/Zanskar (south/west) -> Zanskar Range (central) -> Ladakh Range (parallel to Indus) -> Karakoram (north, hosts Siachen Glacier).
Khardung La = one of the world's highest motorable passes, gateway to Nubra Valley; Chang La = route to Pangong Tso; Zoji La = Ladakh-Kashmir link.
Saser Kangri = Ladakh's highest peak within the Karakoram, exceeding 7,600 m.
